purpose: Prevent fixed-minute horizon claims from conflating event intensity with predictive decay by preserving both clock-time and event-time.
motivation: Order-flow predictability is strongest at short microstructure horizons.
Published multi-horizon evidence reports stock-specific effective forecast horizon of roughly two average price changes, not a universal wall-clock duration.
Taiwan top-five evidence shows predictive heterogeneity by relative tick size, volatility and trading activity.

sourceContract.antiFabrication: OHLCV or sparse snapshots cannot reconstruct event-level OFI/cancellations/replenishment.

dualClock.keyRule: Every 1m/5m/10m/15m/30m research row must retain the underlying event counts and mid-price-change count; horizon comparisons without event intensity are descriptive only.

pressure: true event OFI only with frozen event reconstruction

horizonRetentionProtocol.test: Measure whether standardized Pressure×Response×Persistence information survives after matching/controlling event intensity.
failureInterpretation: If wall-clock alpha disappears after event-count normalization, classify as activity/intensity proxy.
If signal survives only first ~2 price changes and not 10m/15m, keep as execution-state feature, not BUY confirmation.
If 15m retention survives across tick/activity/volatility strata and independent dates, advance to prospective Shadow validation.

sameSlotNormalization.baseline: same symbol + same session-state + same clock slot using prior independent sessions only

coverageContract.unknownRule: Missing/reconnect/serial-gap evidence remains UNKNOWN; absence of message is never zero pressure.
coverageContract.l3Gate: Own Taiwan PIT capture must demonstrate completeness/replay semantics before D05-03/04/05 can be treated as L3.

falsification: Visible depth may cancel; public top-five is not latent full depth.
Positive pressure may be late chase or absorption.
Large-tick and small-tick stocks require separate interpretation.
Deeper-book information may add little beyond best level after costs and controls.
Any predictive effect that is confined to one symbol/date/tick tier is fragile.
